simple.meaning: גְּנַז (gᵉnaz) is a Hebrew object word meaning “treasure.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 5:17. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גְּנַז (H1596) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: גְּנַז (gᵉnaz) / H1596 is traced through Ezra 5:17, Ezra 6:1, Ezra 7:20 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the king’s treasure house, which is there at Babylon, whether it is so, that a decree was made of Cyrus the king to build this house of God at Jerusalem; and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.”

timeline.evidenceText: Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the king’s treasure house, which is there at Babylon, whether it is so, that a decree was made of Cyrus the king to build this house of God at Jerusalem; and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.”
Then Darius the king made a decree, and the house of the archives, where the treasures were laid up in Babylon, was searched.
Whatever more will be needed for the house of your God, which you may have occasion to give, give it out of the king’s treasure house.
